mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day horizon, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a zero drift baseline (p > 0.05), or the Fed rate peak is not sustained for at least 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns within 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < previous value and PAYEMS > previous value by > 10,000 jobs in the same month
failure_condition: In 20-day windows where both PAYEMS and UNRATE move in opposite directions, SPX 20-day returns show no significant correlation with the labor indicators (Pearson IC > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures ( proxy: GDPC1 ) exceeding 2% suggests accelerating demand growth, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 50 such months, the average 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or GDPC1 growth decelerates after the first quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in two consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which can trigger a risk-off spiral and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: In > 40% of such events, the 5-day SPX returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1), or the contraction is followed by rapid recovery within 3 days.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.3% in a month while the Fed funds rate remains unchanged, it suggests inflation stickiness and a higher expected path for future rates, which can depress equity valuations and produce negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change > +0.3% and FEDFUNDS previous month >= current month
failure_condition: In 30 such events, the 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05), or the CPI surprise is followed by immediate rate cuts within 2 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining labor participation rate proxies (not directly available in the catalog; fallback to HOUST for retail employment) combined with flat unemployment suggests a mature labor market, which can lead to risk aversion and negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Over 12 months of such conditions, the 60-day SPX forward return mean is not significantly negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both retail sales (HOUST) and manufacturing activity (RSAFS) exceeding historical averages for three months creates a dual-demand surge that can reinforce equity valuations and drive positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous 3-month avg and RSAFS > previous 3-month avg
failure_condition: In 40 such windows, the 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05), or one of the proxies reverts to below its 3-month average within the next 10 days.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a high-unemployment, low-inflation macro environment (UNRATE > 6.5% and CPIAUCSL < 250) weakens growth expectations and typically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.5% and remains above while CPIAUCSL remains below 250 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: During 20 such regimes, the 60-day SPX forward return mean is not significantly negative (p > 0.05), or the regime persists for less than 6 months.
